title: Coherent integral realization of compactification expressions and their maps
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$,
a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation
ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let
$W$ range over finite-type $k$-schemes and $v$ over separated
finite-type $k$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put
$\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$. Use the abelian category $\mathscr S_W$ of
strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves and its unbounded
derived category, reduction functor $\mathcal R_W$, and total-limit functor
$\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ of
[lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A normalized system has
invertible derived transition-adjoint maps $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$.
Restrict to normalized systems whose levels have compatible etale-origin
witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in
common finite intervals, as in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed,
def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude,
def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. All expressions below are used only when
their intermediate objects have these properties.

On $D(\mathscr S_W)$ use the exact system inverse image $P_v$ and total
right-derived system direct image $S_v$, with $P_v\dashv S_v$ and the
evaluated units and counits of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison].
For an open immersion $j$, use exact termwise $J_j\dashv P_j$.
Tensor is derived tensor over the ring system $((A_n)_W)_n$.
These operations admit their canonical simultaneous ringed-diagram-site
realizations with natural tensor/pullback and composition isomorphisms.
Their pullback composition and tensor isomorphisms are the derived classes
of the canonical maps on flat-term K-flat system resolutions. They obey the
tensor/composition identifications of
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. Direct-image compositors
are conjugate to these pullback compositors under $P_v\dashv S_v$.
For $f=pj$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper, put
$F_f^c=S_pJ_j$ for the chosen compactification $c$
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

The canonical open base-change and tensor maps are normalized as in
[lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The canonical proper/open interchange
for a commutative square of the above schemes
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U&\xrightarrow{k}&V\\
r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ W&\xrightarrow{i}&Z\end{array}$$
with $pk=ir$, open immersions $k,i$ and proper morphisms $r,p$ is an actual
derived system map
$\Gamma_Q:J_iS_r\to S_pJ_k$. After termwise restriction of scalars to
constant $R$-module towers it is the normalized map of
[lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]; its evaluated maps, including
quotient transitions, are the canonical finite proper/open maps. Intrinsically
in $D(\mathscr S)$ it is the adjunct, under the open adjunction
$J_i\dashv P_i$ for the open immersion $i$, of the inverse of the
open-restriction isomorphism $\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\xrightarrow{\sim}S_r$.
Here $\lambda_Q$ restricts $p$ to $q:V_W=V\times_ZW\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]
(open restriction of the direct image, with projection $b:V_W\to V$),
factors $k=bs$ through the induced open-and-closed immersion
$s=(k,r):U\to V_W$, and uses $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$, $J_s\cong S_s$ and the
direct-image composition $S_qS_s\cong S_r$. Thus
$\lambda_Q\circ P_i\Gamma_Q=1_{S_r}$ under the open unit identification.
The horizontal, vertical, base-change, identity and refinement pasting
equations stated in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] hold for
these maps as identities of semilinear-system transformations before
restriction of scalars or evaluation. Thus restriction of scalars is not
being used to detect equality of derived maps. The
coherent system projection and exchange maps are obtained from these
canonical maps and the units and counits by the composites of
[def-exchange-projection].

For derived-complete constructible integral inputs $K_1,\ldots,K_s$, and
any finite well-typed expression $V$ in $P_v,S_p,J_j$ and derived tensor
whose intermediate objects satisfy the bounds above, there are natural
realization isomorphisms
$$c_V:\mathcal L_W V(\mathcal R K_1,\ldots,\mathcal R K_s)
\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{\mathrm{int}}(K_1,\ldots,K_s).$$
Here $V_{\mathrm{int}}$ replaces system pullback and tensor by completed
pullback and completed tensor, $S_p$ by integral proper direct image, and
$S_pJ_j$ by exactly the integral compact-support functor of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The isomorphisms $c_V$
intertwine the canonical system open maps, units, counits, pullback/tensor
and direct-image composition maps, and proper/open interchange with the
corresponding integral maps, including whiskering these maps by any such
expression. In particular this compares nested compact-support functors
and their compactification-composition maps, not only their objects or
finite reductions. The integral open maps thereby equal the localized
ringed-site maps for the completed coefficient sheaves. No lift of an
arbitrary family of derived finite-level arrows, or faithfulness of
derived evaluation on morphisms, is asserted.

The natural realization comparisons for compactification expressions and their generator maps are additional agent-formulated obligations. Blueprint fix-prop-coherence.proof.md: the maps used are tensor reassociation, evaluation, units and counits; this node specifies the coherent lift needed before total inverse limit.

proof.text:
Use the simultaneous semilinear-section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for the operations in the statement. In particular pullback, tensor, open extension, direct image, their adjunctions and coefficient comparisons are constructions on one derived system category, including their morphisms. The evaluated adjunctions are those of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Write $u:1\to\mathcal L\mathcal R$ and $e:\mathcal R\mathcal L\to1$ for the actual unit and counit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. If $N$ is normalized, [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] identifies each $e_{N,n}$ with an isomorphism, the scalar-extension adjoint of the total-limit projection. Since derived evaluations detect isomorphisms, $e_N$ itself is an isomorphism of semilinear systems. This uses detection of isomorphisms only. The limit $\mathcal L N$ is derived complete, and its reductions have precisely the constructibility and common bounds of $N$, by the same counit isomorphisms and [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

For a derived-complete input $K$, [def-weil-derived-complete] gives an isomorphism $K\cong\mathcal L\mathcal R K$: its Roos triangle and the canonical total-limit Roos triangle are triangles of the same reduction tower. This existence statement alone does not identify that isomorphism with $u_K$. Instead, the adjunction identity $\mathcal L(e_N)\circ u_{\mathcal L N}=1$, with $e_N$ invertible, proves that $u_{\mathcal L N}$ is invertible. Take $N=\mathcal R K$, which is normalized by derived tensor reassociation, and use naturality of $u$ along the preceding isomorphism to conclude that the specified $u_K$ is invertible. Thus on the complete/normalized domains we have the specific inverse equivalence with unit $u$ and counit $e$. No arbitrary choice of a morphism between Roos triangles defines a comparison.

proof.text:
Construct the proper/open comparison intrinsically over the ring system, rather than transferring an equality from constant-$R$ towers. In the notation of the item, [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] supplies the geometric fact that $s:U\to V_W$ is clopen. On a pro-etale test object over $V_W$, its inverse images of $s(U)$ and the complementary open cover it disjointly. The sheaf axiom decomposes sections as the product of the two section modules. Projection to the first component and zero on the second is a module map for every $(A_n)$, and commutes with quotient transitions and differentials. This constructs $\pi_s$ directly on semilinear systems. Define
$$\alpha_Q:P_pJ_i\xrightarrow{\beta_{i,p}}J_bP_q\xrightarrow{J_b\pi_sP_q}J_bJ_sP_sP_q\cong J_kP_r,$$
where $\beta$ is the open-unit-normalized system map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Its proper-adjunction mate is
$$\Gamma_Q=(S_pJ_k\varepsilon_r)\circ(S_p\alpha_Q S_r)\circ(\eta_pJ_iS_r).$$
All these are actual system maps by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Taking right adjoints of $P_pJ_i\cong J_bP_q$ gives $P_iS_p\cong S_qP_b$. Consequently $P_iS_pJ_k\cong S_qJ_s\cong S_qS_s\cong S_r$ is the specified $\lambda_Q$: for a clopen immersion $J_s=S_s$, since its section formula is the module on the selected component and zero on the other. Restrict the displayed proper mate along $i$. On $s(U)$ the projection is identity and the proper unit followed by counit cancels by the triangle identity; on its complement $J_s$ is zero. Hence $\lambda_Q P_i\Gamma_Q=1$. The bijection of $J_i\dashv P_i$ now identifies $\Gamma_Q$ with the adjunct of $\lambda_Q^{-1}$.

Here are also the pasting checks inside the semilinear category. For a vertical pasting the two projections select the middle-left open and then the top-left open inside it; their composite is identity on the top-left open and zero on its complement, the outer projection. For a horizontal pasting the projections select the middle open and then its top-left subopen, with the identical component formula. Intersect the two clopen decompositions on each test object to check these equalities component by component. Thus, with the canonical compositors, $\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(\alpha_{Q_1}P_{r_2})\circ(P_{p_1}\alpha_{Q_2})$ vertically and $\alpha_{Q_2Q_1}=(J_l\alpha_{Q_1})\circ(\alpha_{Q_2}J_i)$ horizontally, in the notation of the strict-tower calculus. Base change pulls the selected component and its complement to their inverse images, so it preserves the identity/zero projections and the open-unit comparisons. Taking mates by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives exactly the vertical, horizontal and base-change equations for $\Gamma$ stated there. Identity squares have identity projections, and refinement squares select their clopen section. These componentwise sheaf equations descend to derived semilinear systems by the simultaneous models; no derived restriction or evaluation is used to detect equality. For restriction to constant-$R$ towers use [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] at the sheaf-ring maps $R\to A_n$: inverse image and derived direct image have its canonical scalar-restriction comparisons, with its explicit adjunct identity. The component projection and open extension retain their underlying section maps. Applying these comparisons on the simultaneous section models identifies the restricted mate formula with the constant-$R$ tower mate, including its units and counits. Evaluation then gives the canonical finite normalization specified by the strict-tower calculus. This comparison of defined mates does not use faithfulness of the derived scalar-restriction functor.

proof.text:
For a basic operation $A$, first specify $d_A(K):\mathcal L A\mathcal R K\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathrm{int}}K$ (with two inputs for tensor). For $P_v$ and tensor these are the identifications with the strict reduction-tower formulas of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]: the total limit $\mathcal L_W$ of a strict tower and the cone model $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ on termwise products are identified by the natural Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], the termwise products representing the derived products; the simultaneous models ensure agreement on morphisms and transitions, not merely on evaluated objects. For $S_p$ use the proper direct-image reduction-tower formula of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For $S_pJ_j$, [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] gives the transition from $m$ to $n$: apply $Rp_{*,m}j_!$ to $K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$, then its coefficient-restriction isomorphism. These are exactly the transitions in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The simultaneous system construction and its total limit therefore give $d_{S_pJ_j}$ to precisely that functor, including its maps.

For the standalone open operation the integral realization is the localized ringed-site extension by zero. Its coefficient comparison $r_j:\mathcal R(j_!K)\to J_j\mathcal R K$ is formed by extension by zero on the same K-flat reductions. It is an isomorphism of systems: the open-tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], with the quotient coefficient as the tensor argument, is its evaluation and an isomorphism. It is a coherent map by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The completed open-extension theorem [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] says that this $j_!K$ is complete. Its completeness convention agrees with the quotient-tower convention here: [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies Koszul and quotient completions respecting units, and step 1 identifies the actual quotient-completion unit on complete objects. Hence set $d_{J_j}(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(r_j)^{-1}$. This also identifies the open units with their localized ringed-site units. All opens here are quasi-compact as required by the compactification and finite-type domain. The common constructibility, cohomological and Tor intervals for intermediate values are the explicit domain restriction of the item; no stability theorem with stronger separated-scheme hypotheses is invoked.

proof.text:
Define the comparisons by a genuine induction on expression trees. For a variable $K_i$ put $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$. For a normalized system $M$ at the source of a unary operation $A$, set
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal L M)\circ\bigl(\mathcal L A(e_M)\bigr)^{-1}:\mathcal L A M\longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{int}}\mathcal L M.$$
For tensor use
$$a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal L M,\mathcal L N)\circ\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^L e_N)\bigr)^{-1}.$$
The inverses exist by step 1. If $M=V(\mathcal R K_1,\ldots,\mathcal R K_s)$, define $c_{AV}=A_{\mathrm{int}}(c_V)\circ a_A(M)$. If $M=V(\mathcal R K_i)$ and $N=T(\mathcal R K_i)$, define $c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)\circ a_\otimes(M,N)$. These formulas cover every unary and binary node and decrease tree size at every invocation. Their sources and targets are the stated ones, and each factor is natural and invertible. The induction is legitimate because every intermediate system is assumed normalized, with compatible etale-origin witnesses and common finite cohomological and Tor intervals.

The direct identification $d_{S_pJ_j}$ of step 3 agrees with the recursive composite for $S_p(J_j(-))$. Indeed $r_j$ identifies $\mathcal R(j_!K)$ with $J_j\mathcal R K$ on the very same quotient tower, and the recursion inserts $e_{J_j\mathcal R K}^{-1}$. In the composite the adjacent $\mathcal R\mathcal L$ insertion cancels by $e_{\mathcal R K}\circ\mathcal R(u_K)=1$ and naturality of $e$; the remaining tower is $S_pJ_j\mathcal R K$ with the transitions specified in step 3. The total-limit and resolution comparisons of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] make this an equality of the prescribed comparisons. In particular the recursion does not replace the compact-support definition by an unrelated isomorphic functor.

proof.text:
Check the maps used to build expressions before any assertion based on finite reductions. For a basic operation let
$$r_A(K):\mathcal R(A_{\mathrm{int}}K)\longrightarrow A\mathcal R K$$
be its coefficient comparison in the simultaneous section model. For pullback, tensor, proper direct image and their composites these are the canonical comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; for opens use $r_j$ of step 3. By the counit-transpose clause of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and the definitions of step 3, they are the actual system maps $e_{A\mathcal R K}\circ\mathcal R(d_A(K)^{-1})$, with the analogous two-input formula. This identifies the maps as constructions, rather than concluding equality from their evaluated maps. Repeated substitution defines $r_V$ for a composite expression, and the formulas of step 4 yield
$$r_V=e_{V(\mathcal R K_i)}\circ\mathcal R(c_V^{-1}).$$
For a generator $\tau:V\to T$ we must verify $\tau_{\mathcal R K_i}\,r_V=r_T\,\mathcal R(\tau_{\mathrm{int}})$. Tensor reassociation and pullback composition satisfy this equation on the simultaneous flat-term K-flat resolutions: both send a homogeneous tensor $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ with scalar $a$ acting in the reduced tensor product, and their differentials have the same total-complex signs. For successive pullbacks both apply the composed inverse image and the same structural coefficient maps; their associativity is the associativity of these composites. Their derived comparisons are the specified ones in the item and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For units and counits it is the derived adjunction-transpose identity on those section models, also explicitly preserved by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Direct-image composition is the conjugate of pullback composition; substituting the unit-square and counit-square in the mate formula and cancelling the adjacent unit/counit pairs proves its equation by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting].

For open base change and open tensor, transpose the inverses under the relevant open adjunction. Both sides become the same pullback or tensor comparison applied to the open unit; the open-adjunction Hom bijection proves equality. Thus these are exactly the localized ringed-site maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], including for the completed coefficient sheaves. For proper/open interchange, use the $\lambda_Q$ construction in step 2. Coefficient reduction commutes with its restriction, direct-image composition, and clopen extension/direct-image identification: on the two clopen pieces the latter is identity and zero, respectively. The resulting comparison square for $\lambda_Q$ commutes as a square of system maps. Both interchanges are its inverse's open-adjunction adjunct, so the unit/counit identities already checked give the square for $\Gamma_Q$. Finally projection and exchange are the specified composites of pullback/tensor comparisons, open comparisons, units and counits in [def-exchange-projection]. Substituting the verified squares for those factors gives the square for their composites. The exchange/projection tensor identifications are exactly those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence].

Apply $\mathcal L$ to the generator square. Naturality of $u$, the identity $\mathcal L(e_N)\circ u_{\mathcal L N}=1$, and $r_V=e_{V\mathcal R K_i}\mathcal R(c_V^{-1})$ cancel its outer unit/counit factors and give
$$c_T\circ\mathcal L(\tau_{\mathcal R K_i})=\tau_{\mathrm{int}}\circ c_V.$$
This proves intertwining for the actual integral maps, rather than merely producing maps with the same finite evaluations.

source.place: The maps-used sentence and the statement that coefficient comparisons preserve tensor associativity, evaluations, units and counits; agent verification for the compactification generators.

proof.text:
The generator equation remains true under every allowed expression context. For a unary outer operation $A$, insert the two equations defining $c_{AV}$ and $c_{AT}$ from step 4 and use naturality of $a_A$ at $\tau:V\to T$; the middle square is precisely $A_{\mathrm{int}}$ of the equation in step 5. For tensor with a second expression use naturality of $a_\otimes$ in the chosen slot; if both slots change, factor the map into the two slot maps and use bifunctoriality. Induction on the number of outer nodes proves all the required whiskering equations. Composites of generators are covered because the intervening $c_V^{-1}c_V$ cancel.

Apply this result to the proper/open equations proved inside the semilinear category in step 2. The total-limit functor preserves each equality of transformations. Conjugating by the $c_V$ of step 4 gives its integral identity, with the canonical compositors checked in step 5. In particular the comparison of two nested compactifications is the composite of their direct-image/open compositors and the intervening proper/open generator, so the same calculation proves its compatibility. When compatible composition towers are refined, [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] gives the commuting proper maps on the ambient and intermediate schemes; the corresponding proper/open squares need not be cartesian. Step 2 applies to precisely these general commutative squares, so its vertical and horizontal laws identify the two refined composites. Their common-refinement equalities then survive total limit with the comparisons just proved. This proves the required refinement and nested-composition compatibility; it does not infer an equality from finite evaluations or assert a canonical lift of unrelated finite-level arrows.

proof.text: Naturality follows from the displayed recursion, since $u,e,d_A$ and all the adjunction transposes are natural. For the zero input each additive unary operation and tensor with zero is zero, and the maps into and out of the resulting zero object are its unique maps. For the identity open, its open unit is identity, so the formulas for $\beta,\gamma$ and $\Gamma$ give identity comparisons. For the empty open, $J_j=0$, so those formulas give the unique zero maps. For an identity square the clopen projection is identity and the mate triangle identities give the identity direct-image or open transformation. For an equal-index quotient $A_n\to A_n$, reduction is the identity coefficient map and its comparison is the tensor unit identification. A single compactification is exactly the $d_{S_pJ_j}$ checked in steps 3 and 4. For $W=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and a degree-zero free coefficient module the recursion is ordinary tensor reassociation and the inverse of its reduction-limit unit; rank zero is the preceding zero case. All indices are $n\geq1$; no use of an undefined $n=0$ level occurs. These checks impose no extra geometric or boundedness hypotheses.
